newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bullion seen lower, unnerved by PGMs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bullion seen lower, unnerved by PGMs.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Precious metal markets are likely
to head lower on Wednesday, following overnight trends, with
gold and silver unnerved by volatile PGM markets.
Platinum and palladium were both sharply lower after far
Eastern long liquidation, traders noted.
PLATINUM/PALLADIUM -

Both the key PGMs reversed direction suddenly in the Far East after initially trending higher once more. Heavy losses were prompted by influential long liquidation and profit-taking, ahead of a resumption of Russian shipments of palladium to Japan later this month.
Palladium, which had been as high as $241.00/ounce earlier on Wednesday, was recently indicated at $224.00/$227.00. Platinum fell from levels of $443 to just under $430.
GOLD -
The market is coming under renewed downside pressure from tired long liquidation, prompted partly by the failure of the market to sustain a rally towards the $330 target.
"It really does look as if it will try recent lows," a European analyst said.
Under $320, where prices fell overnight, the market looks vulnerable with intermediate support around $318 and then $315, although the early-July low is $313.60.
"It is really a result of the strong dollar, as well as the huge volatility in the platinum market. This is affecting gold and silver now," the analyst said.
Spot gold was quoted at $318.85/319.25, down some $1.60 from Tuesday's close.
SILVER -
Prices had been moving smoothly higher, but the uptrend was unable to counter the movements in the other industrial white metals, and prices are likely to test $4.30, traders said.
Silver was quoted at $4.33/4.35, down slightly from an overnight close of $4.34/4.36.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
